entries.name: Counterexamples to the pure semisimplicity conjecture and Coxeter type $\mathbb{I}_2(m)$
entries.abstract: Quantum chains of division rings yield counterexamples to the pure semisimplicity conjecture and hereditary artinian rings of every Coxeter type $\mathbb{I}_2(m)$ with $m \geq 4$. For a field element $q$ of multiplicative order $\ell \geq 2$, possibly infinite, the construction gives an extension $H \subseteq T$ with right dimension $2$ and left dimension $\ell$. If $\ell = \infty$, the associated triangular ring is right pure semisimple but neither left pure semisimple nor of finite representation type. Over $\mathbb{Q}$, the parameters $q = 2, 3, 4, \dots$ give pairwise Morita inequivalent counterexamples. If $\ell<\infty$, the ring is of finite representation type with Coxeter type $\mathbb{I}_2(\ell+2)$, and the right dimension sequence of ${}_HT_T$ is periodic with period $(1, 2, \ldots, 2, 1, \ell)$, where $2$ occurs $\ell-1$ times. Every finite $\ell \geq 2$ is realized by choosing $q$ to be a primitive $\ell$-th root of unity.

entries.name: The Large-$N$ Limit of Ricci curvature in the Zeitlin Model on the Torus
entries.abstract: The Euler equations of hydrodynamics describe the motion of an ideal incompressible fluid. Arnold observed that their solutions are geodesics on the group of volume-preserving diffeomorphisms of the fluid domain, equipped with the $L^2$ metric, so that the curvature of this group governs how nearby fluid motions separate. Sectional curvature takes both signs, and Ricci curvature, its average over all directions, is the natural measure of which sign prevails, but in infinite dimensions the sum defining it diverges. When the fluid domain is the flat torus, we define Ricci curvature through Zeitlin's finite-dimensional models, which approximate the Euler equations by geodesic equations on the matrix groups $SU(N)$. We compute the Ricci curvature of these models exactly and prove that, normalized by dimension, it converges as $N \rightarrow \infty$ to an explicit integral. The limit is strictly negative in every Fourier mode and decreases logarithmically with the wavenumber, the behavior conjectured in \cite{lichtenfelz2026ricci} for the sphere. We also show that the diameter of $SU(N)$ in the Zeitlin metric grows at most linearly in $N$.

entries.name: Harper's beyond square-root conjecture for random matrices
entries.abstract: For a Haar unitary matrix $U_N$ of size $N$, we prove that the first absolute moment of $\operatorname{tr}(\operatorname{Sym}^k U_N)$ tends to zero as $\min(N,k)\to\infty$. This settles the random matrix version of Harper's beyond square-root conjecture formulated by Wang and Xu, with no restriction on $k/N$. The proof is elementary and self-contained, combining exact weighted trace moments with a Gaussian change of measure. It also connects the result to the critical chaos model studied by Soundararajan and Zaman, also known as holomorphic multiplicative chaos.

entries.name: Entropy maximization for cube projections
entries.abstract: We prove that, in every dimension $n\ge150$, the one-dimensional projections of the uniform distribution on a cube have the largest differential entropy in directions with equal coordinate magnitudes. This establishes the conjecture of Eskenazis, Nayar, and Tkocz in these dimensions.

entries.name: The bias interval of the elephant random walk
entries.abstract: Guérin, Laulin, Raschel, and Simon conjectured that the initial biases giving the superdiffusive elephant random walk a bimodal limit law form an interval centered at one half, and they described the problem as challenging. We prove this. For every superdiffusive memory, strongly biased starts are unimodal, and the limit density has two local maxima exactly when the bias lies in a proper open interval. Outside it, including its endpoints, the density has a unique local maximum. The interval is nonempty exactly above a single memory threshold, numerically about $0.6688$, whose uniqueness follows from a positive-weight integral for the central curvature of the fair-start density. We control sign changes in the finite walk's first and second differences, including those created at the boundary, and pass them to the limit. The bias boundary is continuous and tends to zero at least quadratically fast as memory tends to one.

entries.name: Integrals over Hilbert schemes and multiple $q$-zeta values
entries.abstract: We establish a version of Okounkov's conjecture on multiple $q$-zeta values arising from integrals over Hilbert schemes of points on smooth projective surfaces. We prove that normalized generating series of integrals involving products of Chern characters of tautological bundles belong to the algebra $\mathcal Z_q$ of multiple $q$-zeta values, without restrictions on the canonical class of the surface. The proof combines vertex-operator methods with a reduction to graph sums, whose arithmetic structure is governed by the cohomology of the surface. We also derive a closed universal formula for the Chern character operators acting on the cohomology of Hilbert schemes by solving a system of differential equations arising from Lehn's commutator relations.

entries.name: Intrinsic reduction data and the loci related to indeterminacy of iterate maps for rational functions
entries.abstract: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of not necessarily characteristic $0$, and $d,n$ be integers $\ge 2$. We first formulate the dynamical moduli spaces of rational functions defined over $k$ in terms of the intrinsic reduction data of non-archimedean rational functions. As an application, we show that the locus $C_{d,n}$ of semistable intrinsic reduction data in degree $d$ whose $n$th iteration is defined and unstable is of codimension $d$ in the intrinsic reduction data space of degree $d$, settling a conjecture of Kiwi and Nie, and show that the image of $C_{d,n}$ in the compactified dynamical moduli $\overline{\mathrm{M}}_{d,k}$ is of dimension $\le d-2$ and the equality holds precisely either if $d$ is even or if $d\ge 5$ is odd and $(4/d)^n<1/(d-3)$ and determine the dimensions even for all the five exceptional pairs $(d,n)$, in addition describing the images of $C_{3,n}$ themselves. We also determine the indeterminacy of iterate maps either on the intrinsic reduction data spaces or on the compactified dynamical moduli spaces.

entries.name: Finiteness of strongly reflective modular forms
entries.abstract: Let $Γ\subset\mathrm{O}^+(n,2)$ be a rational arithmetic group with $n\geq 3$. A non-constant modular form for $Γ$ is called strongly reflective if its zero divisor is a reduced union of mirrors of reflections in $Γ$. We show that, up to conjugation and multiplication by a nonzero scalar, there are only finitely many strongly reflective modular forms. As a consequence, we establish the finiteness of holomorphic automorphic products of singular weight. These results answer a question posed by Borcherds in 1995 and settle a conjecture of Gritsenko--Nikulin from 1998. As an application, up to conjugation, we prove the finiteness of $Γ$ whose corresponding algebra of modular forms is freely generated. The key ingredient is a uniform upper bound on the covolume of $Γ$, obtained by adapting the higher-rank lattice convergence theorem of Abért et al. to the study of the degrees of reflective branch divisors.

entries.name: Congruences involving the products of three binomial coefficients II
entries.abstract: Let $p$ be an odd prime, $a,m\in\Bbb Z_{(p)}$ and $a(a+1)m\not\equiv 0\pmod p$. In this paper, we deduce the congruence for $(\sum_{k=0}^{p-1}\frac{\binom{2k}k\binom ak\binom{-1-a}k}{m^k}) (\sum_{k=0}^{p-2}\frac{\binom{2k}k\binom ak\binom{-1-a}k}{m^k(k+1)})$ modulo $p^3$. As applications we obtain many congruences for \begin{align*}&\sum_{k=0}^{(p-1)/2}\frac{\binom{2k}k^3} {m^k(k+1)^r},\quad \sum_{k=0}^{p-2}\frac{\binom{2k}k^2\binom{4k}{2k}}{m^k(k+1)^r}, \quad \sum_{k=0}^{p-2}\frac{\binom{2k}k\binom{3k}k\binom{6k}{3k}} {m^k(k+1)^r}\quad(r=1,2,3) \\&\sum_{k=0}^{(p-1)/2}k^j\frac{\binom{2k}k^3} {m^k},\quad \sum_{k=0}^{p-1}k^j\frac{\binom{2k}k^2\binom{4k}{2k}}{m^k}, \quad \sum_{k=0}^{p-1}k^j\frac{\binom{2k}k\binom{3k}k\binom{6k}{3k}} {m^k}\quad(j=2,3) \end{align*} modulo $p^3$, which confirm the author's conjectures and improve previous results modulo $p^2$.

entries.name: Modular representations of reductive $p$-adic groups and the kernel of the trace map
entries.abstract: The trace map of a finite group gives a perfect duality between conjugacy classes and irreducible complex representations. For reductive $p$-adic groups, an analogous duality holds due to the classical work of Bernstein, Deligne and Kazhdan. In this paper, we study this trace map for modular representations of reductive $p$-adic groups in characteristic $\ell\ne p$. The failure of the duality is measured by the kernel of the trace map on the cocenter of the ``big Hecke algebra''. Our main theorem expresses this kernel in terms of corresponding kernels for finite-dimensional Hecke algebras associated with normalizers of parahoric subgroups in suitable central quotients of Levi subgroups, reducing a problem on infinite-dimensional algebras to finite-dimensional ones. We also show that projective representations provide a natural complementary subspace on the compact part of the cocenter. For affine Hecke algebras, we prove the naive-kernel conjecture over algebraically closed fields of arbitrary characteristic and for arbitrary compatible nonzero parameters, including unequal parameters and roots of unity.

entries.name: Gamma-positivity of support enumerators of preorders
entries.abstract: The support enumerator of a finite preorder counts lattice points of its polytope by support size. We prove Athanasiadis and Chapoton's conjecture that this polynomial is $γ$-positive. On an $n$-element preorder, the $j$th $γ$-coefficient counts points of the preorder polytope with entries in $\{0,1,2\}$, coordinate sum $n$, and exactly $j$ entries equal to $2$. Oh's correspondence for transversal matroids and Hall's theorem give a formula that records the support itself. For arbors, a separate proof gives a refinement by coordinate sum.

entries.name: A complete solution to the Naor isomorphic reverse isoperimetry conjecture
entries.abstract: For every origin-symmetric convex body $K\subseteq\R^n$, we prove that there exists a volume-preserving linear transformation $T\in\SL_n(\R)$, such that for every $\varepsilon\in (0,1)$ there is an origin-symmetric convex body $L$ with $(1-\varepsilon)TK\subseteq L \subseteq TK$ and the isoperimetric quotient $\iq(L)\le 40\varepsilon^{-1}\sqrt n$. This resolves the Naor isomorphic reverse isoperimetry conjecture.

entries.name: Counterexamples to flagged LLT and nonsymmetric Macdonald atom positivity
entries.abstract: We give a key polynomial of degree fourteen whose expansion in Demazure $t$-atoms has a coefficient with a negative term. This computation disproves the conjectured Demazure atom positivity of flagged LLT polynomials and the corresponding stable atom positivity assertion for modified nonsymmetric Macdonald polynomials.

entries.name: Complex singularities and obstructions to pseudo-Einstein structures: An expository note
entries.abstract: This note explains the counterexamples to Lee's conjecture on pseudo-Einstein structures obtained in joint work with Yoshinori Gongyo, Kengo Hirachi, and Shuya Matsumoto. The examples are links of normal isolated singularities and occur in every odd real dimension at least three. Each link has vanishing first Betti number and vanishing integral first Chern class of its CR structure, yet admits no pseudo-Einstein structure. We explain how finite first homology relates the existence problem on the link to the canonical divisor at the singular point. For the higher-dimensional examples, we describe the key obstruction directly in terms of the first normal derivatives of the transition functions of a line bundle along an exceptional hypersurface.

entries.name: Rohrbach's Conjecture for Finite Groups
entries.abstract: Rohrbach's conjecture holds for finite groups. In fact, there is an absolute constant $C$ such that, for every finite group $G$, every positive integer $h$, and all nonnegative real numbers $α_1,\ldots,α_h$ with $α_1+\cdots+α_h=1$, there are subsets $A_1,\ldots,A_h\subseteq G$ satisfying \[ G=A_1\cdots A_h, \qquad |A_1|\leq |G|^{α_1}, \qquad |A_i|\leq C|G|^{α_i}\quad(2\leq i\leq h). \] Consequently, for every $h$ there is a constant $c_h$ such that every finite group $G$ has a subset $A$ with \[ A^h=G\qquad\text{and}\qquad |A|\leq c_h|G|^{1/h}. \]

entries.name: Ramsey numbers of loose triangles versus cliques
entries.abstract: An $r$-uniform loose triangle $C_3$ consists of three edges that intersect pairwise in exactly one vertex and have no vertex common to all three. For graphs, this is the usual triangle, and the Ramsey number $R(C_3,K_t)$ has order of magnitude $t^2/\log t$ by celebrated results of Ajtai, Komlós, and Szemerédi and of Kim. Kostochka, Mubayi, and Verstraëte proved that $R(C_3,K_t^{(r)})=O_r(t^{3/2})$ for every fixed $r\ge3$ and showed that this bound is sharp up to a logarithmic factor. Motivated by the logarithmic saving in the graph case, they conjectured in 2013 that the upper bound could be improved to $o(t^{3/2})$.This conjecture has since received significant attention and has been reiterated in several papers. We prove the conjecture by showing that, for every fixed $r\ge3$, \[ R(C_3,K_t^{(r)}) =O_r\left(\frac{t^{3/2}}{\sqrt{\log\log t}}\right). \]

entries.name: Non-existence of closed embedded magnetic geodesics
entries.abstract: We give a counterexample to S. Novikov's 1982 conjecture that every Riemannian $2$-sphere contains a closed embedded curve of curvature $c$ for every $c>0$.

entries.name: The Brown--Shields Conjecture: Two Approximation Theorems and a Counterexample
entries.abstract: We construct an outer function in the classical Dirichlet space whose radial zero set has logarithmic capacity zero, but whose polynomial multiples do not approximate the constant function $1$. This disproves the Brown--Shields conjecture. The proof rests on two approximation theorems for canonical generators of invariant subspaces. The first shows that every proper outer canonical generator can be approximated in the Dirichlet norm by canonical generators associated with singular inner functions determined by finite positive atomic measures. The second shows that each fixed finite-atomic canonical generator can be recovered as a strong Dirichlet limit of outer canonical generators whose radial zero sets have arbitrarily small logarithmic capacity. We then combine these approximations using two techniques: a complete metric that controls boundary logarithms and a nested-ball construction that preserves outerness and noncyclicity while ensuring that the radial zero set is polar. In fact, we show that every proper outer canonical generator can be approximated arbitrarily closely by such counterexamples, both in the Dirichlet norm and in the $L^1$ norm of their boundary logarithms.

entries.name: Macroscopic $L^\infty$ bounds for the homogeneous Landau--Coulomb equation
entries.abstract: We establish an instantaneous global $L^\infty(\R^3)$ bound at positive times for smooth, rapidly decaying solutions to the three-dimensional spatially homogeneous Landau equation with Coulomb potential, where the upper bound depends solely on the initial mass, momentum, energy, and entropy. This resolves an open problem posed by Golding, Gualdani, and Loher \cite{GGL} without requiring any initial higher velocity moments, Fisher information, or Lebesgue integrability. The proof builds on two main analytical ingredients. First, we establish the instantaneous generation of the negatively weighted Fisher information with weight $\la{v}^{-1}$. On the lifted two-particle phase space, we compare the separable weight matrix against a collision-invariant pair weight and control the rotational commutator near the diagonal via the quadratic local mass decay supplied by the conserved energy, closing a Riccati differential inequality at the second-moment threshold. Second, to overcome the $\la{v}^{-3}$ radial degeneracy of the diffusion matrix at large velocities, we prove a truncated anisotropic mixed Nash inequality on upper level sets of the density that recovers longitudinal regularity from two transverse Fisher directions and the nonlinear high-density part of the Coulomb entropy dissipation. Localizing this functional inequality to radially aligned velocity cells with the critical weight $\la{v}^{3/2}$ and coupling it with a weighted truncated entropy identity across nested exterior domains yields a superlinear De Giorgi recurrence that bounds the velocity tail uniformly in $\R^3$.

entries.name: Large diameter for $(Δ+2)$-colouring reconfiguration
entries.abstract: Given a graph $G$ and an integer $k$, the reconfiguration graph $\mathcal{R}_{k}(G)$ has the proper $k$-colourings of $G$ for vertices, two of which are adjacent if and only if they differ on precisely one vertex of $G$. In $2022$, Cambie, Cranston and the author proved that the diameter of $\mathcal{R}_{Δ+2}(G)$ is at most $n+2μ$, and put forth a collection of conjectures that in its strongest and most beautiful form would imply that the diameter of $\mathcal{R}_{Δ+2}(G)$ is precisely equal to $n + μ$, for every graph $G$ with $n$ vertices, matching number $μ$ and maximum degree $Δ$. Here we disprove most of those conjectures. Our constructions have reconfiguration diameter at least $n+\frac{3}{2}μ-2$. We also provide counterexamples that are $Δ$-regular, we show that every graph has reconfiguration diameter at least $n+\frac{1}{2} μ$, and we advertise an extension to hypergraphs. It is now much more mysterious how the diameter behaves, so we propose a number of open problems.

entries.name: Why should $\mathbb{Z}$ be Diophantine in $\mathbb{Q}$?
entries.abstract: We give a Diophantine definition of the integers in the rational numbers conditional on the $abc$ conjecture, Dickson's conjecture, and finiteness of $2$-primary parts of Shafarevich--Tate groups. We also discuss some consequences of the existence of a Diophantine definition of the integers in the rational numbers. The goal of this work is to serve as an entry point to recent developments around Hilbert's tenth problem for the rational numbers.

entries.name: From Metric to Strong Metric Regularity: A Second Subderivative Criterion for Definable Prox-regular Subdifferentials
entries.abstract: We investigate when metric regularity of a subdifferential mapping rules out multiple local inverse branches and therefore upgrades to strong metric regularity. Let $h:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,\infty]$ be proper, lower semicontinuous, definable, prox-regular, and subdifferentially continuous at $(\bar x,\bar v)\in\operatorname{gph}(\partial h)$. We characterize this ``upgrade'' through the second subderivative $q = \mathrm{d}^2h(\bar x|\bar v)$ of $h$. If $\partial h$ is metrically regular, then it is strongly metrically regular if and only if the set of negative curvature directions of $q$ on the unit sphere of $\operatorname{span}(\operatorname{dom}(q))$ has Euler characteristic $0$ or $2$. We also prove a simpler and directly verifiable sufficient condition: nonnegativity of $q$ on the lineality space $\operatorname{dom}(q)\cap(-\operatorname{dom}(q))$ forces a quadratic lower bound for $q$ on its entire domain and hence yields strong metric regularity. In particular, if $\bar x$ is a local minimizer and $\bar v=0$, the second subderivative is nonnegative on its domain $\operatorname{dom}(q)$, which proves a conjecture of Drusvyatskiy, Mordukhovich, and Nghia in the definable setting. The derived principle strengthens this conjecture by replacing local minimality with a weaker second-order condition on the lineality space.

entries.name: New bounds on the boxicity of Kneser graphs
entries.abstract: For a graph $G=(V,E)$, the boxicity $\operatorname{box}(G)$ is the least integer $d$ such that $G$ is the intersection graph of axis-parallel boxes in $\mathbb{R}^d$. The Kneser graph $K(n,k)$ is the graph whose vertex set corresponds to the family of $k$ sized subsets of an $n$ sized ground set, and a pair of vertices are adjacent if and only if the corresponding sets are disjoint. In this short paper, we provide new bounds for the boxicity of $K(n,k)$. We first show that for $k\ge 2$ and $n\ge 2k+1$, $\operatorname{box}(K(n,k))\ge n-2k$, thereby improving the lower bounds of Caoduro and Lichev [Discrete Mathematics 346(5):113333 (2023)] when $n\geq 3k+1$ and $k\ge 3$. The proof of this result uses the topological method and follows a strategy similar to Greene's proof of the Kneser's conjecture on the chromatic number of $K(n,k)$. We also show that for $k\ge 2$, $t\ge 1$ and $n=2k+t$, $\operatorname{box}(K(2k+t,k)) \leq O( t^3\log(2k+t) ).$ In particular, for every $t=t(k)\ge1$ with $t^3\log k=o(k)$, $\operatorname{box}(K(2k+t,k))=o(k)$. This is the first upper bound on the boxicity of $K(n,k)$ that is sublinear in $n$. We also show that for large enough $k$, $\operatorname{box}(K(2k+1,k))\le \frac{3\ln (2k+1)}{\ln\ln (2k+1)}$.

entries.name: Matching statistics in regular hypergraphs and applications
entries.abstract: For fixed $k\ge3$, we determine the first sublinear correction to the logarithm of the matching partition function for a class of $n$-vertex $d$-regular $k$-uniform hypergraphs, uniformly for activities in each fixed compact interval of $(0,\infty)$.Our hypotheses include every regular linear hypergraph of polynomial degree and a class of nonlinear hypergraphs described by higher codegrees and intersection patterns, which we introduce here. The weighted counting estimate implies an averaged version of Kahn's conjecture: under the uniform measure, the expected number of uncovered vertices is $(1+o(1))nd^{-1/k}$, with concentration and large deviations on this scale. The proof combines a novel variant of random greedy counting, based on short stages and regular completions, with a new entropy method that uses intersection patterns to control reconstruction after deleting matching edges. We highlight the following applications. (i) Partial transversals in Latin squares. Every Latin square of order $n$ has $(n/e^2)^n\exp((3+o(1))n^{2/3})$ partial transversals. Also, almost all partial transversals have $(1+o(1))n^{2/3}$ missing cells. (ii) Linear $3$-uniform hypergraphs. There are $(n/e^2)^{n^2/6}\exp((1/2+o(1))n^{5/3})$ linear $3$-uniform hypergraphs on $[n]$, and almost all have $n^2/6-(1/6+o(1))n^{5/3}$ edges. (iii) Matroids of fixed rank. For each fixed $r\ge4$, the number $m(n,r)$ of rank-$r$ matroids on $[n]$ satisfies $\log m(n,r)=\frac{n^{r-1}}{r!}(\log n-r+1)+\left(\frac1{(r-1)!}+o(1)\right)n^{r-1-1/r}$, refining the estimates of van der Hofstad, Pendavingh and van der Pol.

entries.name: On the maximum of Poissonian log-correlated fields
entries.abstract: We consider stationary log-correlated random fields of the form \[ X_n(t):= \sum_{j\le n} f(e^{τ_j} t+ v_{j})\,,\quad t\in \mathbb{R} \] for a centered 1-periodic analytic function $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$, where $(τ_j)_{j\ge1}$ are the arrival times of a rate-1 Poisson process on $\mathbb{R}_+$ and $(v_j)_{j\ge1}$ are iid uniform random variables in $[0,1)$. We show that with high probability, \[ \max_{t\in[-1,1]}X_n(t) = c_1 n + c_2 τ_n- (c_3+o(1))\log n \] where $c_1,c_2,c_3$ are positive constants depending on $f$. In particular, the random frequency $τ_n$ produces a central limit fluctuation of order $\sqrt{n}$, together with a logarithmic correction different from the ubiquitous Bramson correction for models with strong comparisons to Gaussian fields, such as homogeneous branching random walks and log-characteristic polynomials of C$β$E matrices. Our proof makes a connection with branching random walks in random time-environment, where coarse-scale fluctuations of the arrival times $τ_j$ play the role of a quenched random environment, and fine-scale fluctuations are leveraged to establish a branching decorrelation structure. We conjecture analogous asymptotics for the characteristic polynomials of random permutation matrices, and expect the same mechanism to arise in other Poissonian fields such as characteristic polynomials of sparse random matrices.

entries.name: Radiation and persistent shape dynamics for the five-dimensional energy-critical nonlinear wave equation
entries.abstract: We consider the nonradial five-dimensional focusing energy-critical wave equation. We construct a forward-global solution which remains arbitrarily close to a nondegenerate sign-changing stationary state in the energy space and is asymptotic to a varying stationary profile plus one free wave. The stationary profile moves in a compact conformal family, but its limit set contains a continuum of classes modulo translations, dilations and rotations. Consequently, the solution admits no soliton resolution using a fixed finite collection of stationary profiles and fixed Lorentz velocities, with pairwise orthogonal spatial parameters. That is, we disprove the fixed-profile soliton resolution conjecture for the five-dimensional focusing energy-critical wave equation. The construction uses a sequence of incoming waves with summable energies. Their quadratic impulses produce fixed shape displacements on increasing time scales. The main estimates control the zero eigenvalue of the linearized operator and the nonlinear error uniformly over the entire sequence. The stationary input uses a computer-assisted spectral bound for a symmetric single-node state.

entries.name: Triameter, distance packings, and vertex connectivity
entries.abstract: We study upper bounds for the triameter of a connected graph in terms of distance packings and vertex connectivity. For any positive integer $k$, we bound the triameter of a graph by a linear function of its $k$-packing number and show that this bound is tight for all values of the parameters. As a corollary, we confirm the conjecture of Das and Abdioğlu on the upper bound for the triameter in terms of the order and the minimum degree of a graph. We also find the maximum triameter among graphs with given order and vertex connectivity, and describe the extremal graphs. Our main tool is a projection of a graph onto a spider or a unicyclic graph which preserves the distances between three prescribed vertices.

entries.name: Toward the abelian category of positive Lagrangians
entries.abstract: We introduce a geometric construction whose terminal configuration determines the kernel and cokernel of a morphism between positive Lagrangian branes in the derived Fukaya category of a Calabi-Yau manifold. Thus, if the construction always terminates, the full subcategory of positive Lagrangian branes is abelian, as conjectured by Joyce. We show that this abelian category admits Harder-Narasimhan filtrations with respect to the central charge defined by the holomorphic volume form. Under appropriate split-generation assumptions, we construct a Bridgeland stability condition whose stable objects are isomorphic to special Lagrangian branes, as predicted by the Thomas-Yau conjecture. The geometric construction is based on a one-parameter family of special Lagrangian submanifolds with boundary. One part of the boundary is contained in the Lagrangian underlying the domain of the morphism and the other in the Lagrangian underlying the codomain. Surgeries occur as the family encounters singularities or obstruction walls. We prove that the construction always terminates for the two-torus and provide higher dimensional examples.

entries.name: $C^{1,α}$ Regularity of $W^{2,2}$ $Q$-Valued Maps with Small Laplacian
entries.abstract: We establish a regularity criterion for $Q$-valued maps $u\in W^{2,2}_{\mathrm{loc}}(Ω,\mathcal A_Q(\mathbb R^k))$, where $Ω\subset\mathbb R^n$ is open. If $|Δu|\leqδ_*|D^2u|$ almost everywhere, with $δ_*=δ_*(n,k,Q)>0$ sufficiently small, then $u\in C^{1,α}_{\mathrm{loc}}$ for some $α=α(n,k,Q)>0$, with quantitative estimates. The result holds for arbitrary $n\geq2$, $k\geq1$, and $Q\geq1$. The proof establishes uniform energy decay using a rigidity principle for positive-semidefinite matrix-valued measures with an aperture bound and approximately atomic divergence, extending the target-stress argument for the homogeneity gap in \cite{Luc26}. The argument relies only on first variation identities. As consequences, we obtain $C^{1,α}$ regularity for Dirichlet-stationary $W^{2,2}$ maps and for locally Lipschitz $W^{2,2}$ maps whose graph varifolds are stationary and have sufficiently small slope. Combining the latter result with Bellettini's Lipschitz sheeting theorem \cite{Bel25}, we establish $C^{1,α}$ sheeting in the multiple-valued sense for two-sided stable minimal immersions whose singular set has vanishing $2$-capacity relative to the immersion, under suitable flatness and mass bounds. Our results allow us to reduce the proof of compactness within this class, under locally uniform mass bounds, to the conjecture that branch sets of stationary $C^{1,α}$ multiple-valued graphs in codimension one have vanishing $2$-capacity.

entries.name: Graded unitarity constraints on simply-laced affine Kac--Moody algebras
entries.abstract: We investigate constraints imposed by four-dimensional unitarity (recently formalised as graded unitarity) on possible simply-laced affine Kac--Moody vertex algebras arising from four dimensions via the SCFT/VOA correspondence. Under the assumption that the $\mathfrak{R}$-filtration is weight-based with respect to the currents and the Casimir operators, with appropriately shifted $R$-charge assignments for the latter, we demonstrate that all values of the level other than a discrete set are incompatible with four-dimensional unitarity. This set includes all the boundary admissible affine vertex algebras, those corresponding to rank-one Kodaira SCFTs, as well as certain non-admissible families conjecturally associated with specific $D^b_q(\mathfrak{g})$ Argyres--Douglas theories. Specialising to $\mathfrak{sl}_N$ with $N$ prime, we find a stronger result: under the same $\mathfrak{R}$-filtration assumption, four-dimensional unitarity rules out all levels except the boundary admissible $k = k_{N,q}$, which are precisely those corresponding to the $D_q^N(\mathfrak{sl}_N)$ Argyres--Douglas theories.

entries.name: Sasakian Hodge Numbers of Calabi-Yau Links
entries.abstract: The link of an isolated weighted homogeneous hypersurface singularity whose degree equals the sum of its weights is a Sasakian manifold that admits a contact Calabi-Yau structure, and its Sasakian Hodge numbers are dimensions of graded pieces of the Milnor algebra of the defining polynomial. In earlier work these numbers were computed with Gröbner bases for the $7$-dimensional links of $7549$ of the $7555$ weighted Calabi-Yau threefold links, and two conjectures were raised from the data. The first asserts that polynomials with the same weights have Milnor algebras whose relevant graded pieces have equal dimensions; the second asserts that the Sasakian Hodge number $h^{2,1}_S$ of the link is bounded above by the Hodge number $h^{2,1}$ of the base Calabi-Yau threefold. Both conjectures are proved here. The first holds for every polynomial with an isolated singularity, because its partial derivatives form a regular sequence; an independent derivation of the Sasakian Hodge numbers by sheaf cohomology on the leaf-space orbifold is also given. For the second, the stringy Hodge numbers of the Calabi-Yau orbifold are shown to bound the middle Sasakian Hodge numbers in every dimension $n\ge2$, and for $n\ge3$ the gap in $h^{n-1,1}$ is shown to be a sum of geometric genera of loci of orbifold points; for threefolds the bound is attained exactly when all curves of orbifold points are rational. The resulting closed formulae give the Sasakian Hodge numbers of the six $7$-dimensional links left open in the earlier work and complete datasets for all $95$ five-dimensional K3 links and all $1\,100\,055$ nine-dimensional Calabi-Yau fourfold links; for the K3 links they recover the previously known second Betti numbers.

entries.name: A new tautological relation on $\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{2,14}$ in cohomology
entries.abstract: We construct a relation $\mathsf{Q}$ in the cohomological tautological ring $\mathsf{RH}^*(\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{2,14})$ which lies outside the space of $3$-spin relations. $\mathsf{Q}$ is a simple linear combination of pure boundary strata classes of codimension 9 supported on the divisor $Δ_0 \subset \overline{\mathcal{M}}_{2,14}$ of irreducible nodal curves, and transforms according to the irreducible representation of $Σ_{14}$ associated to the partition $(2^7)$. The result shows that the set of $3$-spin relations cannot be complete in cohomology. Motivic conjectures relating algebraic cycles to special values of $L$-functions suggest that $\mathsf{Q}$ is nonzero in Chow. More precisely, we prove that the Chow nonvanishing of $\mathsf{Q}$ follows from a conjecture of Harder concerning the failure of the Manin--Drinfeld principle in genus 2. We prove that $\mathsf{Q}$ vanishes in cohomology by pairing with generators of the tautological ring. To prove $\mathsf{Q}$ is not in the set of $3$-spin relations requires an argument involving the $Σ_{14}$-representation-theoretic properties of the $3$-spin relations and the cohomology of local systems on $\mathcal{A}_2$ and $\mathcal{M}_2$. Parallel constructions for other moduli spaces $\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{g,n}$ are discussed in the paper. There are many open questions.

entries.name: On the Hofer-Zehnder conjecture for Reeb flows without symmetry
entries.abstract: This paper continues our investigation of the Hofer-Zehnder conjecture for dynamically convex, non-degenerate Reeb pseudo-rotations of $S^{2n-1}$. The main result of the paper is that, for $n\geq 3$, such a flow has at most $n-3$ alternating prime closed orbits and hence at most $2n-3$ prime closed orbits in total. In particular, the flow on $S^5$ has exactly three prime closed orbits, all of which are non-alternating and elliptic. In addition, we prove that a dynamically convex Reeb pseudo-rotation on a sphere has at least two non-degenerate, irrationally elliptic orbits.

entries.name: The Triangular Abrikosov Constant and the Thomas--Fermi $Γ$-Limit of Rotating Bose--Einstein Condensates
entries.abstract: We resolve the Abrikosov coefficient conjecture for rapidly rotating two-dimensional Bose--Einstein condensates within the variational framework of $Γ$-convergence. For a harmonic trap, we establish the $Γ$-convergence of the rescaled Gross--Pitaevskii energy functionals in the fast-rotation regime, through weak $L^2$ convergence of the rescaled densities, and identify the effective interaction coefficient $β_*$ with $b_\triangle$, the Abrikosov ratio associated with the triangular vortex lattice. The limiting Thomas--Fermi functional determines the first correction to the minimum energy and the macroscopic density of almost minimizers. For the auxiliary rescaled model and its lowest-Landau-level restriction, we also compute a strictly positive limiting $L^2$ distance between minimizing densities and the Thomas--Fermi profile. The identification of the effective interaction coefficient $β_*$ with the triangular Abrikosov ratio $b_\triangle$ relies on the sharp Gaussian-minorant theorem established in a recent OpenAI preprint~\cite[Theorem~1.2]{Atomic}. A Fourier representation of the quartic energy and a weighted Poisson identity yield a lower bound for arbitrary magnetic-periodic lowest-Landau-level states. The sign conditions on the minorant and its Fourier transform give the bound, while the lattice contact conditions identify its coefficient with $b_\triangle$. Cutoff and magnetic projection transfer this estimate to local holomorphic states without boundary conditions or periodicity assumptions. Consequently, the free-cell coefficients converge to $b_\triangle$ with error $O(L^{-1/5})$ on squares of side length $L$.

entries.name: A proof of the Jamneshan-Tao conjecture by embedding nilspaces in nilmanifolds
entries.abstract: We prove that every compact finite-rank nilspace admits a continuous injective morphism into a toral nilspace of the same step, and hence into a connected filtered nilmanifold. Combining this embedding theorem with the general nilspace inverse theorem, we establish the Jamneshan-Tao conjecture and extend its conclusion to second-countable compact abelian groups. This yields an inverse theorem for Gowers norms on all such groups, in which the correlating functions factor through morphisms into nilmanifolds. The proof relies on substantial foundations developed in nilspace theory over the past decade, particularly the general nilspace inverse theorem and the representation of compact finite-rank nilspaces as quotients of free nilspaces.

entries.name: Counterexamples to the clamped-plate eigenvalue ratio conjecture
entries.abstract: Ashbaugh in 1999 conjectures that the ball maximizes the ratio of the second to the first eigenvalue for the vibrating clamped-plate problem. We disprove this conjecture by constructing smooth connected domains in every dimension $d\ge2$. The construction starts with an interior sphere on which the displacement is required to vanish. The first two eigenvalues have the same relative increase at first order, but the second increases more at second order. This gives a strict increase of their ratio, which survives approximation of the sphere by finitely many codimension-two supports and their replacement by smooth holes. We identify the limiting Sobolev spaces through trace estimates and logarithmic cutoffs, and use the geometric construction for the buckling problem to obtain connected perforated domains.

entries.name: The Gaps Between the $Δ$-Unknotting Number and Its Lower Bounds
entries.abstract: Let $u^Δ(K)$ denote the $Δ$-unknotting number of a knot $K$, and let $a_2(K)$ denote the second coefficient of the Conway polynomial. It is known that $u^Δ(K)\geq |a_2(K)|$. We define the $Δ$-gap of $K$ by $G^Δ(K):=u^Δ(K)-|a_2(K)|$. In this paper, we investigate the behavior of this invariant for various families of knots. For example, we prove that the $Δ$-gap of the pretzel knot $K=P(2s, 4s-1,4s+1)$, where $s$ is a positive integer, satisfies $G^Δ(K) \geq 4s$. Consequently, the $Δ$-gap is unbounded. To further investigate the structure of the $Δ$-gap, we distinguish between $Δ$-moves that increase $a_2(K)$ and those that decrease it, since each $Δ$-move changes $a_2(K)$ by $\pm1$. We analyze how these two types of moves contribute to the $Δ$-gap. We also investigate the gaps between $u^Δ(K)$ and other knot invariants that provide lower bounds for it. In particular, we establish explicit formulas and lower bounds for these gaps for certain families of pretzel knots, torus knots, two-bridge knots, and Montesinos knots. Our results show that these gaps can be arbitrarily large. In addition, we identify prime positive knots with $u^Δ(K)=2$ or $3$, and propose a conjecture on a lower bound for $u^Δ(K)$ for prime positive knots.

entries.name: Numerical verification for harmonic maps: Counterexamples to Eells' conjecture
entries.abstract: This paper develops a framework to construct harmonic maps $S^3 \rightarrow S^2$ numerically, which is used to construct approximate harmonic maps in homotopy classes with Hopf invariant $2,3,4,5,6$. By using a rigorous fixed-point argument, it is shown that there exist genuine harmonic maps with the same Hopf invariant close to these approximate solutions, thus producing a family of counterexamples to Eells' conjecture, and the related Ding's conjecture.

entries.name: Refined random matrix conjectures for zeros of $p$-adic $L$-functions
entries.abstract: We make and test the conjecture that for $p$-adic $L$-functions associated to quadratic Dirichlet characters and their Teichmüller twists, all local statistics of zeros in the unit disk match those of $p$-adic random matrix eigenvalues. This generalizes the case of the number of zeros in the unit disk previously conjectured by Ellenberg-Jain-Venkatesh, which was well-supported by numerics, as well as the case of the discriminant, where their numerics were more ambiguous. Using recent random matrix results on local statistics of eigenvalues, we make the random matrix prediction explicit for many statistics, analogous to local densities and pair-correlations in the complex setting. To test these, we compute data on $p$-adic $L$-functions for characters of conductor up to $10^7$, and for certain statistics in windows above $10^{10}$. We find good agreement with the new random matrix predictions for these statistics, as well as for the discriminant.

entries.name: The non-stationary $\widehat{\mathfrak{gl}}_N$ affine Laumon function and its difference equation
entries.abstract: We present an explicit $q$-Givental type formula for the $\widehat{\mathfrak{gl}}_N$ non-stationary affine relativistic Toda or affine Laumon function introduced by Shiraishi. We prove the conjecture of [J. Shiraishi, Affine screening operators, affine Laumon spaces and conjectures concerning non-stationary Ruijsenaars functions. J. of Int. Systems, 4 (2019)], that this function obeys a non-stationary difference equation involving an operator $\widehat{\mathcal T}$, which represents a quiver automorphism (Dehn twist) of the quantum cluster algebra of the affine $A_{N-1}^{(1)}$ Q-system.

entries.name: On configurations that are nearly generalised polygons
entries.abstract: Payne (1972) introduced nearly generalised $n$-gons as $(s+1)$-regular bipartite graphs of girth $2n$ with small excess over the Moore bound. Biggs and Ito (1980) proved nonexistence of such graphs if $s > 1$ and $n > 3$, leaving open the existence of regular antipodal planes. We revisit this problem from several equivalent viewpoints. First we show that a regular antipodal plane of order $s$ is equivalent to a balanced weighing matrix whose support is the incidence matrix of a biplane with parameters \[ 2-\left(\frac{s^2+s+2}{2},\,s+1,\,2\right). \] This gives short determinant and local-arithmetic obstructions to existence. We then formulate the question of signing a biplane as an affine linear system over $\mathbb F_2$, and use this formulation to prove that no regular antipodal plane of order $s$ exists with $4\le s\le 14$. Finally, we give further equivalent formulations in terms of sharply deranged families of permutations and mutually orthogonal array-bic squares. These translations provide new computational and structural approaches to Payne's conjecture that regular antipodal planes exist only for $s=2,3$.

entries.name: Ergodicity without monotonicity: patch-positive spin systems
entries.abstract: Monotonicity is the standard tool for proving that an interacting particle system is ergodic. What can replace it when the system is not monotone and its invariant measure is unknown? The simplest such systems are kinetically constrained models such as FA-1f and East exposed to noise. In these models vacancies enable updates, so adding vacancies should help the system forget its initial state. We prove this for a broad class of spin systems, which we call patch-positive. If vacancies are created spontaneously at a uniformly positive rate, the system converges to the same equilibrium from a large class of initial states, and from every initial state if the threshold density is at most $\tfrac12$ or the interactions are oriented. In particular, the East model with noise is ergodic at every density, and we obtain new cases of the positive-rates conjecture. The key idea is to compare the dual processes of the system with and without the added deaths.

papers.name: Holomorphic vector fields and rationality
papers.abstract: We prove Carrell's conjecture that a smooth complex projective variety with a holomorphic vector field having a nonempty finite zero set is rational. The proof uses slices for projective additive group actions and a birational invariant in the dimension-graded Grothendieck ring. For a vector field with one zero, we bound the second Betti number by the dimension of the kernel of the linear part at that zero. A multiplicative group that normalizes the additive action with a nontrivial character gives a product formula for the Betti numbers and a sharp upper bound for the Euler characteristic. We classify smooth projective surfaces admitting a holomorphic vector field with exactly one zero. Among smooth projective threefolds of Picard number one admitting a holomorphic vector field with exactly one zero, there are five isomorphism types.

papers.name: The Gromov-Lawson-Rosenberg Conjecture for Z/4xZ/4
papers.abstract: We prove the Gromov-Lawson-Rosenberg Conjecture for the group Z/4xZ/4 by computing the connective real k-homology of the classifying space with the Adams spectral sequence and two types of detection theorems for the kernel of the alpha invariant: one based on eta-invariants, closely following work of Botvinnik-Gilkey-Stolz, and a second one based on homological methods. Along the way, we determine differentials of the Adams spectral sequence for classifying spaces involved in the computation, and we study the cap structure of the Adams spectral sequence for sub-hopf algebras of the Steenrod algebra relevant to the computation of connective real and complex k-homology.

papers.name: Triangulations of the 3-sphere with knotted edge
papers.abstract: We prove that for any knot $K$, there exists a one-vertex triangulation of the $3$-sphere containing an edge forming $K$. The proof is constructive, and based on fully augmented links. We use our method to produce ``complicated'' simplicial triangulations of the $3$-sphere that we show are smallest possible, up to a constant multiplicative factor.

papers.name: Rubik's Abstract Polytopes
papers.abstract: We generalize the Rubik's cube, together with its group of configurations, to any abstract regular polytope. We discuss general aspects, and provide a description of the group of the Rubik's simplex in arbitrary dimension, and of Rubik's tori. We sketch an analogous argument for the Rubik's hypercube as well.

papers.name: Exact module categories over $\mathrm{Rep}(u_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2))$
papers.abstract: We give a complete list of indecomposable exact module categories over the finite tensor category $\mathrm{Rep}(u_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2))$ of representations of the small quantum group $u_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$, where $q$ is a root of unity of odd order. Each of them is given as the category of representations of a left comodule algebra over $u_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ explicitly presented by generators and relations.

papers.name: Hodge-Riemann polynomials
papers.abstract: We show that Schur classes of ample vector bundles on smooth projective varieties satisfy Hodge--Riemann relations on $H^{p,q}$ under the assumption that $H^{p-2,q-2}$ vanishes. More generally, we study Hodge--Riemann polynomials, which are partially symmetric polynomials that produce cohomology classes satisfying the Hodge--Riemann property when evaluated at Chern roots of ample vector bundles. In the case of line bundles and in bidegree $(1,1)$, these are precisely the nonzero dually Lorentzian polynomials. We prove various properties of Hodge--Riemann polynomials, confirming predictions and answering questions of Ross and Toma. As an application, we deduce Schur log-concavity of derivative sequences of products of Schur polynomials, confirming conjectures of Ross and Wu. We also prove monomial log-concavity of derivative sequences of dually Lorentzian polynomials. In an appendix, Shouda Wang uses this result to give a new proof of the Dowling--Zhao conjecture.

papers.name: General coupling-based f-divergence diagnostics for Markov chain Monte Carlo
papers.abstract: A long-standing gap exists between the theoretical analysis of Markov chain Monte Carlo convergence, which is often based on statistical divergences, and the diagnostics used in practice. We introduce the first general convergence diagnostics for Markov chain Monte Carlo based on a broad class of f-divergence, allowing users to directly monitor, among others, the Kullback-Leibler and the chi-squared divergences as well as the total variation distance. Our approach rests on a coupling-based 'weight harmonization' scheme that produces direct, computable, and consistent importance weights for interacting Markov chains with respect to their target distribution. Beyond their use as convergence diagnostics, these weights give unbiased estimates of the Radon-Nikodym derivative between the un-normalized target and the distribution of the current iterate, a richer object than the convergence bounds alone, with natural applications to importance-weighted inference. We show how such weightings can provide asymptotic upper bounds to any f-divergence, prove that these bounds converge to zero as the chains approach stationarity, and demonstrate that, while more conservative than existing coupling-based total variation estimators, our method remains a practical and broadly applicable diagnostic tool.

papers.name: On the sharp multi-bubble stability for fractional Hardy--Sobolev equations: a quantitative approach in low dimensions
papers.abstract: We establish sharp quantitative multi-bubble stability for nonnegative critical points of the fractional Hardy--Sobolev inequality in the low-dimensional regime $2s<N<6s-2t$. For functions whose energy is close to that of a finite superposition of bubbles, we prove that the Euler--Lagrange deficit controls linearly the distance, in the homogeneous fractional Sobolev norm, to the multi-bubble set, and we recover the precise bubble configuration. This yields quantitative rigidity under arbitrary finite weak interactions. The proof combines a localization scheme adapted to the Hardy weight, Kato--Ponce type weighted commutator estimates, a bubble-wise spectral gap inequality, and a sharp bubble-bubble interaction analysis. We also show that the linear rate is optimal by constructing a matching counterexample.

papers.name: Similarity-Sensitive Entropy under Representation Change and Inference
papers.abstract: Similarity-sensitive entropy measures the uncertainty of a probability law relative to a similarity kernel that encodes the distinguishability of states. We develop the measure-theoretic treatment covering both finite similarity matrices and general probability spaces, and study how the law and similarity kernel transform under measurable maps, channels, and conditioning operations. This yields data-processing inequalities, so a reduction in entropy quantifies how much distinguishability is lost under representation change. We also define a conditional similarity-sensitive entropy theory, give a counterexample to a recent conjecture on concavity, and identify a practical one-dimensional Laplace kernel class where concavity holds.

papers.name: Descent properties for an abelian variety with extended Galois representation
papers.abstract: Let $K$ be a field, $L$ a finite Galois extension of $K$, and $X$ an abelian variety defined over $L$. If $X$ is isogenous over $L$ to an abelian variety defined over $K$, then the $\ell$-adic Galois representations associated to $X$ extend to representations $\barρ_{\ell,X}:\mathrm{Gal}(\bar{L}/K)\to\mathrm{Aut}(V_\ell X)$ for every prime $\ell$. This paper aims to show that the converse is true for abelian varieties of Type I, with some supplementary conditions needed on the endomorphisms of $X$, when $L$ is either a number field or a function field of prime characteristic different from $2$.

papers.name: Bestvina metric and tree reduction for $K(π,1)$-conjecture
papers.abstract: We reduce the $K(π,1)$-conjecture for all Artin groups to properties of Artin groups whose Coxeter diagrams are trees, from which we deduce new classes of Artin groups satisfying the $K(π,1)$-conjecture. This relies on constructing actions of Artin groups on Bestvina complexes of suitable Garside groupoids.

papers.name: From Trees to Tripods: Proof of $K(π,1)$ for Artin groups with $ABI$-type spherical parabolics
papers.abstract: We describe contractibility criteria for typed simplicial complexes modeled on Coxeter diagrams. Such complexes include buildings and also arise as coset complexes of groups with strongly admissible parabolic systems, including Shephard groups, which generalize both Artin and Coxeter groups. Our result applies to a large class of complexes modeled on \emph{tree Coxeter diagrams} and implies deformation retraction onto a nonpositively curved subcomplex. As an application, we reduce the $K(π,1)$-conjecture for all Artin groups with tree Coxeter diagrams to properties of Artin groups with tripod-shaped Coxeter diagrams. Combining this reduction theorem and properties of braid groups in previous works of Charney, Crisp-McCammond, Haettel and the second named author, we deduce that the $K(π,1)$-conjecture holds for every Artin group whose spherical parabolic subgroups avoid type $D_n$ ($n \ge 4$) and the exceptional types. We give an analogous tree to tripod reduction for Shephard groups. Our proof relies on two ingredients of independent interest: a notion of combinatorial convexity and a Bestvina-type inequality in certain injective orthoscheme complexes. These ingredients further rely on the use of structural properties of bi-Helly graphs developed in joint work of the first named author with Munro.of bi-Helly graphs (also known as absolute bipartite retracts) developed in joint work of the first named author with Munro.

papers.name: Central Limit Theorems for Common Zeros via Bergman Kernels
papers.abstract: We prove central limit theorems as \(N\to\infty\) for common-zero statistics of \(k\) independent standard Gaussian holomorphic sections of \(L^N\), where \(L\) is a positive Hermitian holomorphic line bundle over a compact Kähler manifold of complex dimension \(m\). For fixed real \(\mathscr C^3\) forms \(\varphi\) of bidegree \((m-k,m-k)\) with \(\partial\bar\partial\varphi\not\equiv0\), we prove the CLT in codimensions \(2\leqslant k\leqslant m\) and show that the integrated coefficient in the Shiffman--Zelditch variance formula at scale \(N^{2k-m-2}\) is strictly positive. Shiffman and Zelditch proved the unconditioned smooth CLT for \(k=1\). For \(1\leqslant k\leqslant m\) we also prove a CLT for weighted volumes in fixed domains \(U\) with \(\mathscr C^2\) boundary and fixed real \(\mathscr C^3\) weights \(f\) whose restriction to \(\partial U\) is not identically zero. The variance of a weighted volume is asymptotic to \(N^{2k-m-1/2}ν_{m,k}\int_{\partial U}f^2\,\mathrm dσ\), with \(ν_{m,k}>0\) the Shiffman--Zelditch boundary constant and \(σ\) the induced surface measure. For \(k=m\) and \(f\equiv1\), the statistic counts common zeros in \(U\). Conditioning each section to vanish on the same fixed finite set preserves the leading variance and the Gaussian limit for both classes of tests, including smooth tests for \(k=1\). The set may meet \(\partial U\). A Bergman kernel criterion yields variance bounds and the new unconditioned CLTs from a uniform local \(L^2\) Bargmann--Fock limit and integrable off-diagonal derivative bounds.

papers.name: Auto-differentiable data assimilation: Co-learning of states, dynamics, and filtering algorithms
papers.abstract: Data assimilation algorithms estimate the state of a dynamical system from partial observations, where the successful performance of these algorithms hinges on costly parameter tuning and on employing an accurate model for the dynamics. This paper introduces a framework for jointly learning the state, dynamics, and parameters of filtering algorithms in data assimilation through a process we refer to as auto-differentiable filtering. The framework leverages a theoretically motivated loss function that enables learning from partial, noisy observations via gradient-based optimization using auto-differentiation. We further demonstrate how several well-known data assimilation methods can be learned or tuned within this framework. To underscore the versatility of auto-differentiable filtering, we perform experiments on dynamical systems spanning multiple scientific domains, such as the Clohessy-Wiltshire equations from aerospace engineering, the Lorenz-96 system from atmospheric science, the generalized Lotka-Volterra equations from systems biology, and the two-layer quasi-geostrophic model from geophysical fluid dynamics. Finally, we provide guidelines for practitioners to customize our framework according to their observation model, accuracy requirements, and computational budget.

papers.name: Weakly special varieties, Campana stacks, and Remarks on Orbifold Mordell
papers.abstract: We construct the first weakly special surfaces that are not Campana-special, including the complement of the plane curve $x^2y^3 = 1$ in $\mathbb{A}^2$. We prove that the set of $\mathcal{O}_{K,S}$-integral points on this surface is non-dense for every number field $K$ and finite set $S$ of finite places of $K$ if and only if Campana's Orbifold Mordell conjecture holds for $(\mathbb{G}_m, \tfrac{1}{2}[1])$. This basic example carries a natural $\mathbb{G}_m$-action, and the quotient stack is an Artin stack parametrizing points on a C-pair. This leads to the introduction of "Campana stacks", which encode morphisms of C-pairs in a manner analogous to the role of root stacks for integral points satisfying prescribed divisibility conditions.

papers.name: Hodge Structures in Sextic Fourfolds Equipped with an Involution
papers.abstract: To each ternary sextic $f(X_0, X_1, X_2)$ whose associated plane curve is smooth, the Shioda construction attaches a smooth sextic fourfold $X \subset \mathbb{P}^5$ whose defining equation $f(X_0, X_1, X_2) - f(Y_0, Y_1, Y_2)$ is fixed under the involution $ι: (X_0, X_1, X_2, Y_0, Y_1, Y_2) \mapsto i \cdot (Y_0, Y_1, Y_2, -X_0, -X_1, -X_2)$. The induced action $ι^* : H^4(X, \mathbb{Q}) \to H^4(X, \mathbb{Q})$ fixes a Hodge substructure $H \subset H^4(X, \mathbb{Q})$ whose Hodge coniveau is 1. By the general Hodge conjecture, we expect that there should exist a divisor $Y \subset X$ for which $H \subset \ker\left( H^4(X, \mathbb{Q}) \to H^4(X \setminus Y, \mathbb{Q}) \right)$. We verify this prediction in case the Waring rank of $f(X_0, X_1, X_2)$ takes on its minimum possible value, partially answering a question of Voisin (J. Math. Sci. Univ. Tokyo '15).

papers.name: Approximation Algorithms for Matroid-Intersection Coloring with Applications to Rota's Basis Conjecture
papers.abstract: We study algorithmic matroid intersection coloring. Given $k$ matroids on a common ground set $U$ of $n$ elements, the goal is to partition $U$ into the fewest number of color classes, where each color class is independent in all matroids. It is known that $2χ_{\max}$ colors suffice to color the intersection of two matroids, $(2k-1)χ_{\max}$ colors suffice for general $k$, where $χ_{\max}$ is the maximum chromatic number of the individual matroids. However, these results are non-constructive, leveraging techniques such as topological Hall's theorem and Sperner's Lemma. We provide the first polynomial-time algorithms to color two or more general matroids where the approximation ratio depends only on $k$ and, in particular, is independent of $n$. For two matroids, we constructively match the $2χ_{\max}$ existential bound, yielding a 2-approximation for the Matroid Intersection Coloring problem. For $k$ matroids we achieve a $(k^2-k)χ_{\max}$ coloring, which is the first $O(1)$-approximation for constant $k$. Our approach introduces a novel matroidal structure we call a \emph{flexible decomposition}. We use this to formally reduce general matroid intersection coloring to graph coloring while avoiding the limitations of partition reduction techniques, and without relying on non-constructive topological machinery. Furthermore, we give a \emph{fully polynomial randomized approximation scheme} (FPRAS) for coloring the intersection of two matroids when $χ_{\max}$ is large. This yields the first polynomial-time constructive algorithm for an asymptotic variant of Rota's Basis Conjecture. This constructivizes Montgomery and Sauermann's recent asymptotic breakthrough and generalizes it to arbitrary matroids.

papers.name: Explicit Planar Finite Element Elasticity Complexes and $C^1$ Elements on Barycentric Refinements
papers.abstract: We give a closed-form realization of the finite element elasticity complex associated with the Arnold--Douglas--Gupta family on barycentric refinements. Their construction implies the existence of minimal $C^1$ potential spaces, but does not provide explicit general-degree scalar enrichments. On each macrotriangle, we derive three divergence-free stress enrichments and their Airy potentials. For every degree $q\geq4$, the resulting potential space enriches $\mathbb P_q$ by three explicit functions. A geometric decomposition yields unisolvent degrees of freedom and $C^1$ assembly without vertex supersmoothness. The space attains the dimension bound for macroelements containing $\mathbb P_q$ with full polynomial boundary trace freedom. Its Airy image is the divergence-free subspace of the corresponding stress space, and global assembly gives an exact discrete elasticity complex on simply connected domains. The low-order spaces $U_2$ and $U_3$ recover the reduced and full Hsieh--Clough--Tocher spaces, respectively.

papers.name: Frame constructions associated with operator orbits
papers.abstract: This paper studies frames in Hilbert spaces generated by the orbits of finitely many vectors under a single operator, presenting new results on normal operators and multiplication operators as well as on operators composed of Jordan blocks. These results generalize existing results of Cabrelli, Molter, Paternostro and Philipp by means of techniques which deal with weighted interpolation, weighted composition operators, and Beurling--Lax theory related to shifts of finite multiplicity. Likewise, we discuss Carleson frames and construct counterexamples to a recent conjecture of Aldroubi, Cabrelli, Krishtal and Molter, showing that the relevant necessary condition is of density type rather than the Müntz--Szász condition. Moreover, by using the theory of weighted composition operators, we answer a question of Cheshmavar on frames produced by iterative multiplication. Finally, for orbits of infinitely many vectors the underlying model is a shift of infinite multiplicity which, by a theorem of Rota, is a universal operator; consequently, a complete description of such frames along these lines would encompass the Invariant Subspace Problem.

papers.name: On $\mathbb J$-strata with Parahoric Stabilizers in Affine Deligne-Lusztig Varieties
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the $\mathbb J$-stratification of basic affine Deligne-Lusztig varieties for a minuscule cocharacter $μ$. This stratification was introduced by Chen-Viehmann and has been expected to serve as an interesting tool for studying basic loci in Shimura varieties. We parametrize the $\mathbb J$-strata whose stabilizers in the Frobenius-twisted centralizer group are parahoric by constructing a natural bijection to combinatorial invariants called small cocharacters. We further prove that the cardinality of these sets is equal to that of a certain subset of the Weyl group orbit of $μ$. A relationship with the weakly fully Hodge-Newton decomposability of Chen-Tong is also discussed.

papers.name: A unified approach to cross-intersection problems with applications to Hilton--Milner type theorems and stability
papers.abstract: We develop a new approach to cross-intersection problems in extremal set theory. The method builds on the iterative procedure introduced by Kupavskii and Zakharov (2024) and the $t$-cover method. It provides a flexible framework for deriving extremal and stability results for cross $t$-intersecting families. Our approach applies to a variety of combinatorial objects. As an application, we prove a product version of the seminal Erdős--Ko--Rado theorem for sufficiently spread set systems. Two families $\mathcal{F}$ and $\mathcal{G}$ of $k$-subsets of $[n]$ are called cross $t$-intersecting if $|F\cap G|\geq t$ for all $F\in\mathcal{F}$ and $G\in\mathcal{G}$. We determine the families maximizing $\min\{|\mathcal{F}|, |\mathcal{G}|\}$ for large $n$ and all $t\ge2$, generalizing results of Mörs (1985) and Füredi (1995) for cross $1$-intersecting families. We then determine the families maximizing $|\mathcal{F}||\mathcal{G}|$ under the condition $\max\{|\cap_{F\in\mathcal{F}}F|,|\cap_{G\in\mathcal{G}}G|\}<t$ for large $n$. This improves the bound obtained by Frankl and Wang (2024), and provides a characterization of extremal configurations. For a family $\mathcal{F}$ of subsets of $[n]$, we introduce its $t$-diversity $γ_t(\mathcal{F})$, defined as the minimum number of sets from $\mathcal{F}$ not containing a fixed $t$-subset. This serves as a natural generalization of the important notion of diversity for $t=1$. We obtain a stability result via $γ_t$, and determine the maximum of $\min\{γ_t(\mathcal{F}),γ_t(\mathcal{G})\}$ for cross $t$-intersecting families $\mathcal{F}$ and $\mathcal{G}$. These yield new results for $t$-intersecting families, including a stability theorem towards a conjecture of Ellis, Keller and Lifshitz (2019), which may also be regarded as a $t$-intersection version, for large $n$, of an influential theorem of Frankl (1987).

papers.name: On phase-lock area parquet in a special slow-fast limit of model of Josephson junction
papers.abstract: B Josephson (Nobel Prize, 1973) predicted a tunnelling effect for a system of two superconductors separated by a narrow dielectric (such a system is called Josephson junction): existence of a supercurrent through it and equations governing it. The overdamped Josephson junction is modeled by the family of differential equations on the 2-torus, $\frac{dθ}{dτ}=\frac1ω(\cosθ+B+A\cosτ)$, which is known as the RSJ model. It depends on three parameters: $B$ called the abscissa, $A$ called the ordinate, and a fixed frequency $ω$. We study its rotation number $ρ(B,A;ω)$ as a function of $(B,A)$ and the phase-lock areas: those its level subsets that have non-empty interiors. They exist only for integer values of the rotation number (Buchstaber, Karpov, Tertychnyi). In this paper we study asymptotics of the phase-lock area portrait in a special slow-fast limit, as $ω\to0$ and $(B,A)\to(0,1)$ so that $(B,A)-(0,1)=O(ω)$. We show that in the rescaled parameters $\ell:=\frac Bω$ and $u:=\frac{A-1}ω$ the phase-lock area portrait converges to a parquet with boundary lines being parallel to the lines $\{ u\pm\ell=0\}$. Namely, the limit of phase-lock area with rotation number $r$ is the union of an infinite chain of squares going up, with integer vertices and diagonals of length two lying on the line $\{\ell=r\}$, and an infinite strip going down (sector in the case, when $r=0$). We state and prove a generalization of this result to a wide class of slow-fast systems on 2-torus.

papers.name: Deformation of the absolute Galois groups of number fields
papers.abstract: The technical goal of this paper is to construct and study profinite monoids DG_K for number fields K such that (1) the unit group of DG_K is isomorphic to the absolute Galois group G_K; (2) the maximal abelian quotient of DG_K is isomorphic to the Deligne-Ribet monoid DR_K; (3) the idempotents of DG_K bijectively correspond to subsets of the set P_K of (finite) primes of K; (4) the maximal Galois groups G_{K, S} with restricted ramifications S all appear as maximal closed subgroups of DG_K at idempotents; (5) all maximal closed subgroups of DG_K at idempotents are of this form. We also discuss the relationship between DG_K and the p-typical Witt vectors of Borger and de Smit, where we will describe the fundamental monoid of the semi-galois category of Lambda-rings of Borger and de Smit in terms of fields of norms of the local field K_p in particular.

papers.name: Optimal Oracle Complexity for Weakly Convex Optimization
papers.abstract: We study the oracle complexity of finding $ε$-stationary points of $ρ$-weakly convex and $G$-Lipschitz functions, where stationarity is measured by the gradient norm of the Moreau envelope. We consider an exact first-order oracle that returns both the function value and the full subdifferential at every query point. For sufficiently small $ε>0$, we prove that every first-order algorithm, including randomized algorithms, requires $Ω({ρG^2Δ}/{ε^4})$ oracle queries to succeed with any fixed positive probability, where $f(0)-\inf f\leΔ$. This lower bound matches the best known deterministic and stochastic first-order upper bounds, up to universal constants, and establishes the optimal randomized and deterministic first-order oracle complexity. The result separates smooth nonconvex and nonsmooth weakly convex optimization: the additional $ε^{-2}$ factor is intrinsic to nonsmooth geometry rather than to stochastic oracle noise.

papers.name: Risk-Aware Quantile Learning for Personalized Dynamic Treatment Regimes
papers.abstract: Sequential clinical decision-making often involves more than maximizing average efficacy. Clinicians may need to simultaneously optimize clinically relevant tails of the outcome distribution, control treatment-related risk, and choose among multiple treatment options. Existing quantile dynamic treatment regime (DTR) methods capture distributional features of treatment outcomes but remain largely restricted to efficacy-only objectives and binary treatments. To address these limitations, we propose Risk-Aware Quantile Dynamic Treatment Regimes (RQDTR), a unified framework that optimizes a prespecified quantile of the cumulative potential outcome while explicitly incorporating treatment-related risk. We also develop an angle-based formulation for jointly learning decision rules across multiple treatment categories. Our framework includes three interpretable subclasses: efficacy-only quantile learning, constraint-based learning with population-level risk control, and utility-based learning through a composite benefit-risk utility. Theoretically, we establish identification and oracle equivalence, surrogate and estimator consistency under increasing quadratic penalties, asymptotic risk feasibility, and finite-sample performance error bounds. Extensive simulation studies and applications to All of Us major depressive disorder and MIMIC-III sepsis data demonstrate that RQDTR improves tail-oriented efficacy and achieves more favorable benefit-risk trade-offs than existing quantile DTR methods.

papers.name: A constrained Onsager variational framework for parametric approximations of Willmore and Helfrich flows
papers.abstract: We develop a constrained Onsager variational framework for parametric finite element approximations of Willmore and Helfrich flows. The weak curvature relation is used as a PDE constraint to express the first variation of the bending energy in curvature-vector form. Onsager's principle then combines this variation with dissipation based on the normal velocity, while an independent relaxed minimal-deformation-rate (relaxed-MDR) constraint selects the tangential velocity. The resulting mixed formulation admits a semidiscretization by continuous piecewise linear elements that satisfies an exact energy-dissipation law and exactly preserves area and volume when the corresponding constraints are imposed. The framework accommodates constant spontaneous curvature and applies to both closed surfaces and open surfaces with fixed boundaries under Navier or clamped conditions. We also propose a linearly implicit fully discrete scheme, prove its unique solvability, and present numerical experiments demonstrating convergence, energy decay, constraint preservation, and effective mesh redistribution.

papers.name: Kusner's conjecture on equilateral sets is false
papers.abstract: We disprove Kusner's 1983 conjecture that every equilateral set in $\ell_p^n$ with $2<p<\infty$ has at most $n+1$ points: there exist $58$ points in $\mathbb{R}^{56}$ whose pairwise $\ell_5$ distances are all equal, so the maximum equilateral-set size satisfies $e(\ell_5^{56})\ge58>57$. This is the first equilateral set of more than $n+1$ points in $\ell_p^n$ for any finite $p\ge2$. The construction persists on an open interval of exponents around $5$. The configuration is specified by the unique solution of an explicit polynomial system with rational coefficients in a rational box; existence and uniqueness are proved by exact integer inequalities. The existence of the $58$-point equilateral set in $\ell_5^{56}$ has been formalised in Lean from standard axioms.

papers.name: On Samuels' Conjecture
papers.abstract: Let $0\leqμ_1\leq\cdots\leqμ_n$ and let $λ>\sum_{i=1}^nμ_i$. Let $X_1,...,X_n$ be independent nonnegative random variables satisfying $\mathbb{E}X_i=μ_i$, and write $D_i := λ-\sum_{k=1}^{i-1}μ_k$ for $1\leq i\leq n$. We prove that $$ \inf_{X_1,...,X_n} \mathbb{P}\left( \sum_{i=1}^nX_i<λ\right) = \min_{1\leq i\leq n} \prod_{j=i}^n \left( 1-\frac{μ_j}{D_i} \right). $$ The bound is sharp and is attained. This proves Samuels' conjecture. Feige's conjecture is thereby resolved, since it follows immediately from the equal-means case. The proof is self-contained.

papers.name: Exceptional model structures and the induced extriangulated categories
papers.abstract: A Hovey triple $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{F}, \mathcal{W})$ is {\it exceptional}, if $(\mathcal{C} \cap \mathcal{F}, \ \mathcal{C} \cap \mathcal{F} \cap \mathcal{W})$ is not a Frobenius pair. One has a disjoint union $\{\text{Hovey triple}\} = \{\text{Hereditary Hovey triple}\} \ \dot\bigcup \ \{\text{Exceptional Hovey triple}\}$ \ $\dot\bigcup \ \{\text{non-hereditary and non-exceptional Hovey triple}\}.$ Exceptional Hovey triples appear widely. For a selfinjective Nakayama algebra $A= kC_n/J^t$, $A\mbox{-}{\rm mod}$ admits exceptional Hovey triples if and only if $\gcd (n, t) \ge 2$ and $t \geq 3$. Their homotopy categories reveal new phenomena. Nakaoka-Palu's Theorem implies that there is a triangulation on $\frac{\mathcal C\cap\mathcal F}{\mathcal C\cap\mathcal F\cap\mathcal W}.$ It is proved that a Hovey triple in a weakly idempotent complete extriangulated category $(\mathcal A, \mathbb E, \mathfrak s)$ is exceptional if and only if the induced extriangulated structure $\bigl(\frac{\mathcal C\cap\mathcal F}{\mathcal C\cap\mathcal F\cap\mathcal W}, \ \overline{\mathbb E}, \ \overline{\mathfrak s}\bigr)$ is not {\it canonically triangulated}. Between this extriangulated structure and the one arising from the triangulation, the intermediate extriangulated structures are in one-to-one correspondence with Serre subcategories of $\mathrm{fp}((\frac{\mathcal P(\mathcal C\cap\mathcal F)}{\mathcal C\cap\mathcal F\cap\mathcal W})^{\mathrm{op}}, \mathrm{Ab})$.

papers.name: The periodic Wulff problem in two dimensions
papers.abstract: We characterize the minimizers of the anisotropic perimeter in the two-dimensional flat torus under an area constraint. We show that, as the prescribed area increases, global minimizers undergo two phase transitions, changing from a droplet (a rescaled Wulff shape) to a flat band wrapping around the torus in a preferred direction determined by the anisotropy (lamellar phase), and finally to a bubble (the complement of a reflected and rescaled Wulff shape). The transition thresholds are given explicitly in terms of the area and the lattice width of the Wulff shape. For certain non-symmetric surface tensions, the lamellar phase is absent altogether. Finally, we characterize the surface tensions for which further minimizers appear: this may happen only in the lamellar regime, and exactly when the Wulff shape has a corner whose normal cone contains, in its interior, a direction realizing the lattice width; in this case there are infinitely many minimizers.

papers.name: Liouville regular Jordan curves
papers.abstract: We investigate Liouville regular Jordan curves, which were introduced in our previous paper as "Jordan curves that admit continuous Legendrian lifts". We prove that a Jordan curve satisfying certain variation conditions in a neighborhood of each point is Liouville regular. We also prove that the boundary of a Jordan domain is Liouville regular if the images of the radial tails under a conformal mapping have uniformly vanishing length. Together with our previous result, these criteria show that each such Jordan curve admits an inscribed rectangle in every prescribed similarity class.

papers.name: Orthonormal bases of spherical harmonics with maximal Lp norm growth
papers.abstract: In this paper, we show that for every p>2, there is an orthonormal basis of spherical harmonics on the n-dimensional unit sphere which achieves the maximal Lp norm growth. More precisely, one basis achieves this growth for p up to the critical exponent 2(n+1)/(n-1), and another for p from the critical exponent up to infinity. The first basis is built from rotations of the real part of a highest weight spherical harmonic. The second is built from zonal harmonics whose poles are selected from a spherical design. In both cases, the selection uses the restricted invertibility theorem of Bourgain and Tzafriri. This extends earlier results of Bourgain and of the author (arXiv:1404.5016) on the 2-dimensional sphere for 2<p<=6 to all dimensions and all p>2, and improves the positive density subsequence there to a whole basis.

papers.name: Proof of the singularity conjecture for discrete subgroups of $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{R})$
papers.abstract: Let $μ$ be a finitely supported probability measure on $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{R})$ whose support generates a Zariski-dense discrete subgroup. We prove that its stationary probability measure on $\mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{R})$ is singular with respect to the $\mathrm{SO}(2)$-invariant probability measure. The proof compares winding variances on finite covers of a closed hyperbolic surface and uses a topological obstruction.

papers.name: An Equivariant Landweber Exact Functor Theorem for Abelian Compact Lie Groups
papers.abstract: We prove an equivariant Landweber exact functor theorem for abelian compact Lie groups $G$. For a graded module $N$ over the $G$-equivariant Lazard ring $L_G$, we give necessary and sufficient algebraic conditions on $N$ for the functor \[ X\longmapsto (MU_G)_*(X)\otimes_{L_G} N \] to define a homology theory on the category $\mathrm{Sp}^G$ of genuine $G$-spectra. Our criterion is obtained by varifying the Landweber exactness on each stratum indexed by a closed subgroup of $G$ and then gluing the local flatness data via Euler classes. As an application, we show that for any non-equivariant Landweber exact ring spectrum $E$, $MU_G\wedge_{MU} E$ is equivariantly Landweber exact, thereby proving a conjecture of Wisdom. Finally, we study the $G$-equivariant formal groups $\widehat E_G$ over $\hom(G^*,E)$ associated to elliptic curves $E/S$. We prove that its classifying map $\hom(G^*,E)\to\mathcal M_{\mathrm{FG}}^G$ is flat whenever $S\to\mathcal M_{\mathrm{ell}}$ is flat, and recover $\widehat E_G$ from Gepner-Meier's equivariant elliptic cohomology associated to any oriented spectral lifting of $E/S$.

papers.name: Polynomial Decay in Absorbing Continuous-Time Markov Chains
